notes.title: New Trailer!
notes.content:
[h2]Hi everyone. [/h2]
It’s been a while! Get Together is coming along nicely and we took the time to update our current trailer which we used as a marketing material both on steam and social networks. 

[previewyoutube=3n4jw5g7aiE;full][/previewyoutube]

Until now the trailer showed some of the puzzle mechanics, the character(s), hand-crafted sounds and a demo environment. It was quite an important step for us so players really could get a feel for how the game looks, sounds and in the end also plays. The whole scene was an excerpt from an earlier state for first testings and was also used to give ourselves a kind of visual development kickstart to the final production.

Since then we’re knee-deep in said production! Some additional months passed and with it several iterations on character animations, environment creations and puzzle setups. So with the summer almost in reach we thought it’s time to update the trailer with new content and level segments of Get Together. 


So long, thanks for reading and watching.

Until next time,
The Team

PS: Stay tuned for some cool news in the next month!

notes.title: Dev Showcase - Workflow Props
notes.content:
[h2]Hi Everyone. [/h2]

We’re incredibly busy filling the world of Get Together with the planned content we have in mind. So we thought that it might be a good time to give a glimpse of how we do that. First up is a small peek into the production workflow for the props in Get Together.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39406174/28264f2b49c2c98f9ebd38aca8b2d4e3a264538c.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39406174/2be1c5a429cc17be4557ebe6612a41a33d9b54f3.png[/img]

[h3]1. Game Design[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39406174/010d9616be74408b24764ecbbce0a5a578708a77.png[/img]

It all starts with Game Design (Simon) laying out some ideas for a prop, it’s functions and most of the time also the rough size of it as well. In this case the prop is called the ‘Lorestone’. It’s a recurring object which will, you guessed it, tell the Player a little bit about the world and lore of Get Together. 

So the idea is there, functions are laid out and the proportions are estimated: 
Ancient stone that shows some rune-y lore and it’s bigger than the player (but not too big!).

Tools: Google Docs & whatever-painting-software-is-open

[h3]2. Concepts[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39406174/7337b1d789d3fa9be72d655f01c75f144d5d5bb6.png[/img]

Now the pipeline leads to our concept artist (Heinrich), who does a variety of different rough black and white sketches based on the info that are given by game design. We then discuss the selection and further refine a few also applying some color. 
As the ‘Lorestone’ is a recurring prop, Heinrich made sure it would fit in different environments as well.

Tools: Procreate (Heinrich wouldn’t have it any other way, but that’s ok)

[h3]3. Drawing[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39406174/929e4fe679e7fbd320779ce46505275a163797f0.png[/img]

After having a solid concept our main artist (Ally) starts overpainting the asset. While thinking colors, shading and linework, it’s brought to a final state to match the general game’s art style. Things like in-game perspective and proportions compared to existing assets are also being considered. 

The final step includes setting up layers & specific sizes to enable easy export and possible changes (shoutout to compression magic and the Power of Two).

Tools: Photoshop (Yeah we know…)

[h3]4. Implementation[/h3]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/ngaPU2S.gif[/img]

Finally the asset is imported and placed in a Unity scene. Most of the time the process does not end here. Either there are some further iterations happening or more often the asset itself is part of a feature which also includes stuff from other departments. Sometimes the prop is so important that most of the surroundings are created just for this asset, as it is the case with our ‘Lorestone’. Extra Sound, extra VFX, and of course extra Character Animations.

So long, thanks for reading. 

Until next time,
The Team

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39406174/2be1c5a429cc17be4557ebe6612a41a33d9b54f3.png[/img]

notes.title: Introducing Get Together
notes.content:
[h2]Hi Everyone. [/h2]

The steampage for Get Together is online for a few months now, but we have not come around to make a proper post about it. So here it goes…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39406174/9d6eaef7d1cf76edba9907e1b9cd5dc67641ae80.gif[/img]

Get Together is a [i][b]coop puzzle adventure[/b][/i] for two players. Follow the story about a luckless explorer who gets split into two beings. You and a friend take control of these two parts and your goal is as simple as trying to get them back together! 
All [i][b]puzzles are specifically designed to be played by two people[/b][/i]. You both have to exchange information about what you can find in your world, because it sure seems like you two don’t see the same…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/39406174/6dbb2d4f12d1783c4ab1d1f99f4d1d7de48a31bf.gif[/img]

Here’s the best part! You can play [i][b]cross-platform[/b][/i] with your [i][b]mobile devices[/b][/i] and [i][b]no internet connection is needed[/b][/i]. The only thing that's required is the ability to communicate with your partner. Via [i][b]discord[/b][/i], zoom, skype, classic landline or even old-school ‘[i][b]sitting next to each other[/b][/i]’, the means are certainly there!

tl;dr features for the lazy bugs ;)
[list]
[*] Communication-based puzzle adventure exclusively for two
[*] Unique painterly art style and carefully crafted sound world
[*] Easy to learn controls to focus on player-communication
[*] Cross-Platform play on Windows, iOS and Android
[*] No internet connection required to play
[/list]
